findings.title: Mixed-width integer comparison refused (MNE119)
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Resource checks compare memory (i64 MiB/bytes) against counts (i32 CPUs) and version tuples (i32) in one predicate nest.
findings.minimal_reproducer: fn c(env: R) -> (result: bool) { return env.small_i32 <= env.big_i64; } with record R { small_i32: i32, big_i64: i64 } fails elaboration with MNE119 'binary operands must have the same type' (plus MNE163 on the projection). Same-width comparison elaborates and executes.
findings.expected_behavior: Either implicit widening with checked semantics or a diagnostic naming the widths and suggesting an explicit conversion.
findings.actual_behavior: MNE119 hard error; the Fabric module keeps mem_mib/i64 and cpu_count/i32 in separate same-width comparisons and can never write the natural mixed comparison.
findings.migration_boundary: Keep compared quantities at one width per comparison in MNCS; width bookkeeping stays host-side.
findings.next_action: Decide numeric promotion semantics (checked widening) or bless explicit conversion builtins; update the Fabric module to use them.

findings.title: Record argument mismatch reports no expected-vs-actual diff
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Execution corpora pass record values (WorkerEnv, WorkloadReq) to compiled entrypoints.
findings.minimal_reproducer: Emit a record argument whose type_identity uses a single colon before the field spec (record-type:{mod}::{T}:{spec}) instead of the canonical double colon ({T}::{spec}); `experiment run` reports per-case status invalid_request with failure_reason 'argument does not match SSA input type' and no identities.
findings.expected_behavior: failure_reason (or a verbose flag) prints the expected SSA input identity alongside the received type_identity.
findings.actual_behavior: Opaque reason; root-causing required dumping the backend artifact bytes and byte-comparing identities by hand.
findings.migration_boundary: None needed once fixed; corpus builders must byte-compare against `mncs abi` output until then.
findings.next_action: Include expected vs received type identities in the InvalidRequest failure reason for record/finite/sequence arguments.

findings.title: No shared corpus-value builder for record/finite/integer encodings
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Every MNCS corpus hand-rolls finite/record/integer JSON encoders (percent-encoded record-type identities, [name, value] field lists, discriminants).
findings.legacy_path: mncs/gen_*_corpus.py across mncs-fabric; scripts/gen_platform_capability_corpus.py in mncs-language
findings.desired_mncs_path: a toolchain-owned builder (CLI subcommand or documented helper) emitting argument values from `mncs abi` output
findings.minimal_reproducer: Three independent hand-rolled encoders (capability, platform-decision, language platform corpus) with three chances to get the `::` separator, field ordering, or discriminant wrong; P-002 was found this way.
findings.expected_behavior: `mncs` offers one supported way to construct execution-request arguments (or validates a corpus against ABIs with pinpoint diagnostics).
findings.actual_behavior: Copy-paste encoders per module; drift fails at execution time, not authoring time.
findings.migration_boundary: Fabric keeps its local record() helper pinned against `mncs abi` output in tests until the toolchain owns one.
findings.next_action: Ship a supported corpus-argument builder or an `mncs corpus lint` command that validates arguments against ABI contracts.

findings.title: Module imports experimental; Fabric duplicates std platform vocabulary
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Os/Arch/Libc/Accel/ExecMode/Req* enums exist in mncs.std.platform.v1 and are re-declared in fabric.platform_decision.
findings.desired_mncs_path: mncs/fabric_platform_decision.mncs importing mncs.std.platform.v1 and adding only the Fabric composition (env_satisfies over Fabric records)
findings.minimal_reproducer: Profile 0.6 admits import declarations experimentally; cross-module finite/record identity reconciliation for a Fabric consumer of std platform types is unproven in this campaign (the module was written import-free to stay inside the proven envelope).
findings.expected_behavior: Stable imports with nominal finite/record identity reconciliation, so Fabric reuses std types by reference.
findings.actual_behavior: Duplicated declarations pinned arm-for-arm by tests/test_mncs_platform_decision.py; any std evolution must be manually mirrored.
findings.migration_boundary: Duplication is explicit and test-pinned; the import migration is a named follow-up.
findings.next_action: Stabilize module imports for finite/record reuse; then delete the duplicated Fabric enums and re-pin the corpus.

findings.title: No MNCS string/text surface; all classification stays host-side
findings.subsystem: capability classification, version parsing, identity handling
findings.fabric_source_behavior: classify_os/arch/libc/init/accel map unbounded platform strings into finite enums; parse_fabric_version maps version text into tuples; worker/record identities are sha256: text.
findings.desired_mncs_path: bounded-text classification functions inside MNCS over an explicit alphabet
findings.minimal_reproducer: There is no string type in the exercised profile; MNCS never observes raw platform text by construction (host classifies first). A corpus case cannot feed "x86_64" to MNCS at all.
findings.expected_behavior: Bounded, total string handling (or an explicit refused-outside-envelope story) so classification logic itself can be language-owned.
findings.actual_behavior: Classification is permanently host-side; MNCS owns only the post-classification decision. New platform strings can only be handled by editing Python.
findings.migration_boundary: Host classifies; MNCS decides. The boundary is documented per module and a new platform string can never silently reinterpret an MNCS arm.
findings.next_action: Design bounded-text semantics (RFC) before moving any classifier; until then keep the host-classifies/MNCS-decides split.

findings.title: No IO effects: networking, filesystem, processes, clocks, hashing
findings.fabric_source_behavior: EnvelopeTransport request/response, canonical JSON + sha256 identities, RFC 3339 timestamps, ledger files, subprocess execution, bundle transfer.
findings.legacy_path: src/mncs_fabric/transport.py, service_transport.py, canonical.py, evidence.py, receipts.py, store.py, executor.py, bundle_transfer.py
findings.desired_mncs_path: MNCS-owned protocol state machines over host-provided effect capabilities
findings.minimal_reproducer: The exercised profile has no effect/handle surface for sockets, files, processes, clocks, or hashing; spec/effects-and-capabilities.md describes direction but no executable surface was available to this campaign.
findings.expected_behavior: Capability-scoped effects (clock, random, hash, file, socket) with explicit authority so Fabric protocol logic can move into MNCS while the host owns the resource.
findings.actual_behavior: All IO-adjacent semantics stay Python. Evidence hashing and timestamping cannot be language-owned without breaking evidence guarantees.
findings.migration_boundary: MNCS owns pure decisions; every byte, hash, timestamp, and packet stays host-side. No evidence logic was weakened to fit.
findings.next_action: Implement the effects-and-capabilities surface starting with clock/hash/file; Fabric transport is the first consumer.

findings.title: No sets/maps/iteration/sorting; fleet aggregation stays host-side
findings.subsystem: fleet resolution, token-set matching, ledger folding
findings.fabric_source_behavior: resolve_fleet ranks eligible workers (preference hits, resource-constrained flag, lexicographic id); resolve_worker intersects require_all/forbid/prefer token sets; lifecycle stores fold ledger event lists.
findings.desired_mncs_path: MNCS-owned ranking comparator + set-membership predicates over bounded token domains
findings.minimal_reproducer: Bounded sequences/views/vectors exist (profiles 0.7-0.10) but set semantics, string-keyed maps, iteration over capability tokens, and deterministic sorting were not inside this campaign's proven envelope; the pairwise ranking comparator shape was deliberately deferred rather than half-moved.
findings.expected_behavior: Bounded sets/maps with total iteration and a deterministic ordering story so fleet aggregation can be language-owned.
findings.actual_behavior: MNCS owns per-worker classification; aggregation, ranking, and token-set algebra stay Python. Two semantic layers persist (pinned by tests, but two).
findings.stdlib_involved: bounded collections (partially present, unproven for this use)
findings.migration_boundary: Per-worker verdicts are MNCS-pinned; fleet math stays Python until collection semantics land.
findings.next_action: Prove bounded-set/sort patterns for capability tokens (or refuse explicitly); then move resolve_fleet ranking into MNCS.

findings.title: No services/concurrency/event loops; controller/worker cores stay Python
findings.subsystem: controller, worker, supervisor, work queue, heartbeats
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Registration, heartbeats/liveness loops, work acquisition, execution requests, retries, bounded resource handling, update transactions over time.
findings.minimal_reproducer: No async/event-loop, timer, or long-lived-service surface exists in the exercised envelope; even the work-queue tick (pure selection over queued items) needs ledger persistence and clocks first.
findings.expected_behavior: A service story (timers, cancellation, bounded concurrency) sufficient for heartbeat/lease/queue lifecycles.
findings.actual_behavior: All orchestration stays Python. MNCS owns the lifecycle state relations those loops consult (management, update, reconnect, queue-state shapes are next).
findings.migration_boundary: State relations move first (this campaign); the loops that consult them stay host-side.
findings.next_action: Define the service/timer story; candidate first consumer is work-queue tick + liveness lease checks.

findings.title: Per-case execution/observation cost bounds corpus scale
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Exhaustive finite-domain corpora (449 platform + 328 reconnect + 245 update + 84 capability + 70 management + 40 status = 1216 cases) executed per change.
findings.minimal_reproducer: Observed: research-bytecode per-case observation/validation dominates (compile once, pay per case); prior measurement ~2.3 s/case for the deeply-nested 14-state update corpus locally, worse on hosted runners. The four new small-decision modules (887 cases combined) execute in seconds, so cost scales with relation complexity, not just case count; the six-module conformance job keeps a 150-minute timeout for the heavy corpora.
findings.expected_behavior: Sub-second marginal per-case cost (frozen-artifact reuse, cheaper observation) so exhaustive Fabric policies stay in the fast loop.
findings.actual_behavior: PASS on all modules, but wall-clock bounds how large an executable Fabric policy can grow before the edit/execute loop degrades. Conformance stays path-filtered + weekly for this reason.
findings.backend: research-bytecode (frozen-artifact execute shows the same marginal)
findings.migration_boundary: Corpora stay exhaustive; CI stays filtered. No semantic coverage was cut for speed.
findings.next_action: Profile observation/validation cost (canonical-hash volume per trivial case) and add a cheaper execution tier.

findings.title: No host-callable MNCS artifact story; Python stays the runtime authority
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Scheduler, controller, and worker call Python decision functions at runtime; the MNCS modules execute the same relations in CI but nothing calls them in production.
findings.desired_mncs_path: mncs-fabric as an MNCS program/artifact with Python as bootstrap glue; runtime calls into compiled MNCS decisions
findings.minimal_reproducer: There is no supported path in this campaign to load a compiled MNCS artifact from Python (or ship an MNCS-built mncs-fabric executable) with the evidence story intact; `experiment execute` runs frozen artifacts offline but is a conformance tool, not a runtime embedding.
findings.expected_behavior: Aembedding story: host calls named MNCS entrypoints with JSON values, gets values back, with versioned artifact identities recorded in receipts.
findings.actual_behavior: MNCS is the authoring-time and CI-executed authority; Python is the production runtime authority. Two implementations persist by necessity, pinned by tests — exactly the transitional architecture, but the final reversal step has no vehicle.
findings.migration_boundary: Every duplicated arm is corpus-pinned with a named MNCS owner; drift fails tests. Removal of Python arms waits on the embedding story.
findings.next_action: Design the host-embedding contract (call argparse, value encoding, identity recording); pilot it on resolve_code, the smallest hot decision.

findings.title: Only research-bytecode exercised; WASM/C11/LLVM/Cranelift unproven for new modules
findings.fabric_source_behavior: Six Fabric MNCS modules executed on research-bytecode only.
findings.desired_mncs_path: same corpora PASS on portable-wasm-mvp, C11, LLVM, Cranelift
findings.minimal_reproducer: No multi-backend run was attempted in this campaign; profile 0.6 claims broad realization, but Fabric evidence covers one backend. `mncs experiment matrix` is the machine-readable envelope source, not consulted here.
findings.expected_behavior: Nightly/weekly multi-backend execution of the Fabric corpora with backend-specific failures recorded separately (per mission).
findings.actual_behavior: Single-backend evidence. A feature working only because research-bytecode accidentally supports it would go unnoticed.
findings.migration_boundary: None; evidence is honestly single-backend until the matrix runs.
findings.next_action: Add a weekly multi-backend matrix job over the six Fabric corpora; file backend findings separately from language findings.

findings.title: No Option/None semantics; absent values stay host-side
findings.fabric_source_behavior: freshness_of(None) means live-derived (fresh); management_allows_work(None) means unknown-but-schedulable; artifact None means unverified rather than mismatched.
findings.desired_mncs_path: explicit option types so absence is a value MNCS can match on
findings.minimal_reproducer: MNCS entrypoints take non-optional enums/bools; every None folds to a host-side default before the call (documented per module). There is no way to pass 'absent' and let MNCS decide what absence means.
findings.expected_behavior: Option types with exhaustive matching so absence policies (live-derived freshness, unknown-state scheduling) are language-owned.
findings.actual_behavior: Absence policies live in Python glue; MNCS sees only present values. The split is documented and pinned but the policy boundary is drawn by the type system gap.
findings.migration_boundary: Each module documents its None-folding; corpora pin the present-value arms.
findings.next_action: Add option types (or an explicit absence story); migrate the three absence policies first.
